```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
    collapse = TRUE,
    comment = "#>",
    message = FALSE,
    warning = FALSE
)
```

`edger.bp` runs edgeR-compatible analyses on genes-by-samples count matrices
stored with BPCells. It is intended for pseudobulk matrices where the number of
genes is large enough that row-blocked GLM fitting and file-backed storage are
useful.

The package does not define new statistical methods. It mirrors supported edgeR
workflows for BPCells-backed matrices, so statistical choices should follow the
edgeR documentation.

## Data Contract

Inputs should satisfy the usual edgeR count-matrix requirements:

* rows are genes or features;
* columns are samples or pseudobulk sample-cluster columns;
* entries are non-negative integer counts;
* row names and column names are present and unique;
* `nrow(design)` equals the number of matrix columns;
* optional `group` values are aligned to the matrix columns.

For large analyses, create the BPCells matrix before calling `edger.bp`. Keep a
column metadata table alongside it with any sample, cluster, batch, or donor
fields needed to build design matrices.

## A Small Runnable Example

The example below simulates a small two-group pseudobulk experiment and writes
the counts to a temporary BPCells directory.

```{r simulate}
library(edger.bp)
library(BPCells)
library(Matrix)

set.seed(7)

ngenes <- 120L
nsamples <- 8L
group <- factor(rep(c("ctrl", "stim"), each = 4L))

base_mean <- rgamma(ngenes, shape = 2, rate = 0.15)
fold_change <- rep(1, ngenes)
fold_change[seq_len(12L)] <- 2.5

counts <- vapply(seq_len(nsamples), function(j) {
    mu <- base_mean * ifelse(group[[j]] == "stim", fold_change, 1)
    as.integer(rnbinom(ngenes, mu = mu, size = 8))
}, integer(ngenes))

rownames(counts) <- paste0("gene", seq_len(ngenes))
colnames(counts) <- paste0("sample", seq_len(nsamples))

bp_dir <- tempfile("edger-bp-counts-")
sparse_counts <- Matrix(counts, sparse = TRUE)
sparse_counts <- BPCells::convert_matrix_type(sparse_counts, "uint32_t")
bp_counts <- BPCells::write_matrix_dir(sparse_counts, dir = bp_dir)

design <- model.matrix(~ group)
colnames(design)
```

The audited package versions can be checked explicitly:

```{r versions}
bp_check_versions(error = FALSE)
```

## Likelihood-Ratio Test

`bp_lrt()` runs preparation, optional filtering, TMM normalization, dispersion
estimation, and blockwise GLM LRT testing. The returned object keeps those
stages separate.

```{r lrt}
lrt_fit <- bp_lrt(
    bp_counts,
    design = design,
    group = group,
    coef = "groupstim",
    dispersion.method = "stream",
    block.size = 50L,
    workers = 1L
)

names(lrt_fit)
head(lrt_fit$lrt$table[order(lrt_fit$lrt$table$PValue), ])
```

Important components are:

* `prepare`: filtered counts, library sizes, normalization factors, and offsets;
* `dispersion`: common, trended, and tagwise dispersion estimates;
* `lrt$table`: the edgeR-style result table for the requested coefficient or
  contrast.

## QL F-Test and Treat

`bp_qlf()` and `bp_treat()` use edgeR's modern quasi-likelihood path by default.
They can also accept a supplied scalar or gene-level dispersion vector when that
matches the intended edgeR analysis.

```{r qlf}
qlf_fit <- bp_qlf(
    bp_counts,
    design = design,
    group = group,
    coef = "groupstim",
    dispersion.method = "stream",
    block.size = 50L,
    workers = 1L
)

head(qlf_fit$qlf$table[order(qlf_fit$qlf$table$PValue), ])
```

`bp_treat()` tests whether the effect exceeds a log2 fold-change threshold. The
default threshold follows edgeR's `glmTreat()` default, `log2(1.2)`.

```{r treat}
treat_fit <- bp_treat(
    bp_counts,
    design = design,
    group = group,
    coef = "groupstim",
    dispersion.method = "stream",
    lfc = log2(1.2),
    block.size = 50L,
    workers = 1L
)

head(treat_fit$treat$table[order(treat_fit$treat$table$PValue), ])
```

For legacy edgeR quasi-likelihood comparisons, use `qlf.args` or `treat.args`:

```{r legacy, eval = FALSE}
bp_qlf(
    bp_counts,
    design = design,
    group = group,
    coef = "groupstim",
    qlf.args = list(legacy = TRUE)
)

bp_treat(
    bp_counts,
    design = design,
    group = group,
    coef = "groupstim",
    treat.args = list(legacy = TRUE)
)
```

## One-vs-Rest Marker Tests

A common marker workflow builds one binary design per cluster. The pseudobulk
matrix still has genes as rows and pseudobulk columns as samples; only the design
changes.

```{r one-vs-rest, eval = FALSE}
cluster <- col_data$cluster
selected <- cluster == "cl01"
design_marker <- model.matrix(~ selected)

marker_cl01 <- bp_treat(
    bp_counts,
    design = design_marker,
    group = selected,
    coef = "selectedTRUE",
    lfc = log2(1.2),
    block.size = 1000L,
    workers = 4L
)

marker_table <- marker_cl01$treat$table
```

This binary one-vs-rest design directly compares the selected cluster to all
other columns pooled together. A shared `~ 0 + cluster` design with contrasts can
be faster for many clusters, but it is a different estimand and should be chosen
deliberately.

## Storage Order and Parallelism

BPCells matrices have a physical storage order. Column-ordered storage is useful
for sample-wise operations such as library sizes and TMM normalization. Row-
ordered storage is useful for blockwise gene operations. If you need a companion
matrix with the other storage order, use `bp_ensure_storage_order()`.

```{r storage-order, eval = FALSE}
bp_counts_row <- bp_ensure_storage_order(
    bp_counts,
    order = "row",
    outdir = "cache/counts_row",
    tmpdir = "cache/tmp"
)
```

The main tuning arguments are:

* `block.size`: number of genes materialized per edgeR block;
* `workers`: number of row blocks processed in parallel where supported;
* Slurm resources: for full datasets, run package workflows in batch jobs and
  budget memory as roughly proportional to `workers * block.size * ncol(y)`.

Small interactive checks should use `workers = 1L` or `2L`. Full pseudobulk
marker runs should use Slurm and an explicit wall-time/QoS choice appropriate to
the cluster.

## Full-Scale Workflow

A typical full-scale analysis is:

1. Build or load a genes-by-pseudobulk BPCells count matrix.
2. Load column metadata and construct the design matrix.
3. Run a small smoke test on a subset of genes or clusters.
4. Run the full workflow with recorded `block.size`, `workers`, package
   versions, and Slurm resources.
5. Save the result table plus enough metadata to reproduce the design and
   contrast.

For example:

```{r full-scale, eval = FALSE}
bp_counts <- BPCells::open_matrix_dir("cache/counts_col")
col_data <- read.delim("cache/sample_metadata.tsv")

group <- factor(col_data$condition)
design <- model.matrix(~ group)

fit <- bp_treat(
    bp_counts,
    design = design,
    group = group,
    coef = "grouptreated",
    block.size = 1000L,
    workers = 8L
)

write.table(
    fit$treat$table,
    file = "results/edgeR_treat.tsv",
    sep = "\t",
    quote = FALSE,
    col.names = NA
)
```
